title: MS HB1723: Artificial intelligence; define.

reading.body:
Mississippi's HB1723 adds a definition of "artificial intelligence" to the Mississippi Code, effective July 1, 2026, and imposes no duties, restrictions, or penalties on anyone.

The definition is broad, covering machine-based systems that make predictions, recommendations, or decisions for human-defined objectives, using machine and human inputs to perceive environments, abstract them into models, and use model inference to formulate options. Because the act contains no obligations, prohibitions, or enforcement provisions, it creates no compliance steps and has no direct effect on AI deployment in Mississippi.

What the data does not show is whether future Mississippi legislation will attach requirements to this definition. The act is silent on who it applies to, any exemptions, and any penalties, so it cannot be read as imposing operational requirements on AI systems or the infrastructure that runs them.

What it does

This act defines the term 'artificial intelligence' for use in the Mississippi Code. It does not impose any duties, restrictions, or penalties.

Who it applies to

  • Not stated in the text

Effective date

July 1, 2026

Key definitions

  • artificial intelligence: a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations or decisions influencing real or virtual environments; artificial intelligence systems use machine- and human-based inputs to perceive real and virtual environments; abstract such perceptions into models through analysis in an automated manner; and use model inference to formulate options for information or action (Sec. 1)

Obligations

  • None stated in the text

Prohibitions

  • None stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

Not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • The act only defines 'artificial intelligence' and imposes no direct obligations, prohibitions, or penalties on organisations deploying AI (Sec. 1, Sec. 2, Sec. 3).

Notable exemptions

  • None stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • No compliance steps are required because the act only defines a term and does not impose duties (Sec. 1).

Full text of the law

MS HB1723, 1048 characters, as enrolled. Public record.

MISSISSIPPI LEGISLATURE 

 2026 Regular Session 

 To: Technology 

 By: Representatives Ford (73rd), Scott 

 House Bill 1723 

 (As Sent to Governor) 

 AN ACT TO DEFINE THE TERM "ARTIFICIAL
INTELLIGENCE"; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES. 

      BE IT ENACTED BY THE
LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MISSISSIPPI: 

      SECTION 1.  
The term "artificial intelligence" means a machine-based system that
can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions,
recommendations or decisions influencing real or virtual environments. 
Artificial intelligence systems use machine- and human-based inputs to perceive
real and virtual environments; abstract such perceptions into models through
analysis in an automated manner; and use model inference to formulate options
for information or action. 

      SECTION 2.   Section 1
of this act shall be codified in Chapter 3, Title 1, Mississippi Code of 1972. 

      SECTION 3.  This act
shall take effect and be in force from and after July 1, 2026.
